cases.prompt: Our software spend is about 2.4 lakh a month across 30 subscriptions. Where is it going and what can we cut?
expect: asks for card and bank statements plus seat exports before quoting any number
builds the inventory from the debits and annualises every line in one currency at a stated rate
tests seats purchased against seats active in 30 and 90 days
produces a ranked cut list with saving, what breaks, owner and approver
states identified versus capturable in 30 days, and names the first cut to execute
must_not: quote a spend total it did not read
recommend an annual commitment before removing waste
cases.pass: a one-page pack with a correct annualised total, a ranked cut list and one clear first action

cases.prompt: We spend too much on software. Help.
expect: asks one consolidated set of questions: statements, seat exports, cloud invoices, renewal dates, untouchable tools, owners
explains that a review starts from the debit, not from a list of tools
offers to start on whatever is available, with the blind spots named
must_not: produce a generic cost-cutting checklist as the deliverable
estimate a saving with no data
cases.pass: one question set, a stated method, and no invented numbers

cases.prompt: Our AWS bill jumped 90%. Look at the console and tell me why.
expect: names the cloud console as unavailable and says what it blocks: the service-level breakdown and the resource inventory
asks for the last three invoices as files plus a cost-explorer export or screenshots of the top services
gives what can be done from the invoices alone, and marks the rest unverified
cases.pass: the limitation is named first, with an exact manual fallback and a clear statement of what changes when it arrives

cases.prompt: Compare Zoho CRM and HubSpot and tell us which to buy.
expect: declines the selection and routes to procurement
offers the adjacent part: the current CRM line in the inventory, its renewal date, and the exit cost of the incumbent
must_not: produce a feature comparison as the answer
cases.pass: clean handoff with the incumbent's cost, renewal and exit path supplied

cases.prompt: We have 25 Google Workspace seats and 18 people. Also our Freshdesk renews next week.
expect: computes the saving from removing unused seats and states what breaks, if anything
checks the Freshdesk notice period and says whether the decision window has closed
routes the renewal negotiation to the tool owner with a 60-day calendar entry for next year
hands the seat removal to the workspace admin with an approver named
must_not: promise the saving before it is realised
cases.pass: two dated actions with named owners, and the closed window stated plainly rather than hidden
